findings.construct: pub struct MetricWorkflow { pub status: String, pub is_validated: bool, pub is_sent: bool, ... }
findings.problem: MetricWorkflow uses status: String plus two lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent) instead of an enum typestate. This permits illegal state combinations like status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with is_sent=true and no sent_at_epoch.
findings.failure_mode: Any code checking item.status == "sent" ignores the booleans entirely, while code checking is_sent ignores the status string. No invariant enforces a consistent lifecycle. The struct represents an unbounded state space including states that should be impossible.
findings.fix: Replace the three fields with a single `State` enum: `enum State { Created, Validated { validated_at_ms: u64 }, Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 } }`. Remove status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms. Make mark_sent consume the validated variant and return Sent.

findings.problem: Raw String for workflow status. Status is a domain concept that must be an enum to make illegal states unrepresentable.
findings.failure_mode: Arbitrary strings like "SENT", "", "sent_pending" compile and pass any equality check. No compiler enforcement of valid transitions.
findings.fix: Replace with a `State` enum (see typestate_enum_required finding). Remove the String field entirely.

findings.problem: Lifecycle boolean on struct. Booleans encoding lifecycle phases must be transitions inside an enum variant.
findings.failure_mode: is_validated can be true while is_sent is also true, with no recorded sent_at_epoch, or status could be something other than "sent". The boolean carries no proof of when validation occurred.
findings.fix: Fold lifecycle data into enum variants: `State::Validated { validated_at_ms: u64 }`. The presence of the variant encodes the boolean.

findings.problem: Lifecycle boolean on struct. Same as is_validated — must be an enum variant, not a bare bool.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent can be true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or with status != "sent". No invariant ties the flag to timestamp or status.
findings.fix: Replace with `State::Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 }`. The variant presence encodes is_sent and the timestamp lives inside the variant.

findings.problem: Optional lifecycle timestamp on a struct that already has is_sent: bool. Option outside the state machine decouples the timestamp from its lifecycle gate.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent=true and sent_at_epoch_ms=None is a valid struct, representing a sent metric with no record of when. Conversely is_sent=false but sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(...) is also valid.
findings.fix: Move the timestamp inside the Sent enum variant as a required field: `State::Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 }`. The Option disappears because the variant cannot exist without the value.

findings.problem: MetricWorkflow ID is a bare String with no domain constraints. No uniqueness, format, or length rules encoded in the type.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicate IDs, and non-metric identifiers all type-check. No compile-time distinction between a MetricWorkflow ID and any other string.
findings.fix: Introduce a `MetricId` newtype: `pub struct MetricId(String);` with a smart constructor that validates format/length. Use `MetricId` as the field type.

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: MetricWorkflow) -> MetricWorkflow
findings.problem: mark_sent takes a fully-formed MetricWorkflow and mutates fields directly. No smart constructor validates preconditions or returns typed errors. The function silently accepts any state and overwrites status string.
findings.failure_mode: Calling mark_sent on a MetricWorkflow that hasn't been validated (is_validated=false) is a domain violation with no compile-time or runtime enforcement. The function also loses the original sent_at_epoch_ms if it was Some.
findings.fix: Define mark_sent as `fn mark_sent(state: State) -> Result<State, TransitionError>` that consumes the validated state variant and returns Sent. Remove the struct-level mutation entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() allocation and direct field mutation. In a typed-domain design the state transition would be a pure function from one enum variant to another with no String allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Every call allocates a new String for the status field even though the value is always the same literal "sent". With a State enum the Sent variant would be zero-allocation.
findings.fix: Replace with enum-based transition: `State::Validated { validated_at_ms } => State::Sent { sent_at_ms }` — zero allocation, no String, no .to_string().

findings.construct: No benchmark module or criterion/criterion-like dependency
findings.problem: No benchmark exists for any performance claim or allocation analysis. The mark_sent function allocates a String on every call which is suboptimal for a hot path.
findings.failure_mode: Without a baseline benchmark, there is no evidence that the allocation in mark_sent matters, or that replacing it with an enum variant actually improves performance.
findings.fix: Add a criterion benchmark for mark_sent on a representative workload. After typestate refactor, benchmark again to measure allocation elimination.

findings.construct: No test, clippy, or fmt evidence
findings.problem: No tests, no clippy run, no cargo fmt check. The review is static only.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that the proposed typestate refactor compiles or passes lint gates. Cannot confirm current code meets clippy strictness.
findings.fix: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy` with strict lint gates, and `cargo test` to establish a verification baseline before and after any refactor.

missing_evidence: no clippy or cargo check evidence
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands were executed. The struct as written permits all illegal state combinations through status/is_validated/is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms independence. The typestate enum refactor fully eliminates these illegal states at compile time. Without running clippy and cargo check, lint-level compliance is unverified.
